facts.raw_span: subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts
subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The patient has violaceous cutaneous lesions consistent with leukemia cutis and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis.
The patient has nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots and a high white blood cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis, consistent with leptomeningeal disease.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, consistent with a neurological disorder.

The patient has violaceous cutaneous lesions consistent with leukemia cutis, nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis, consistent with neurolymphomatosis.

rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are a characteristic feature of leukemia cutis, which is a type of leukemia.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is suggestive of leptomeningeal disease or neurolymphomatosis.
rationales.F11: A high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid is indicative of leukemia or lymphoma, which can cause leptomeningeal disease or neurolymphomatosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis) and a cell differential with 98% atypical cells/blasts strongly support leukemia, which can also explain the neurological findings through potential leptomeningeal involvement.
